guide.aab.caution: A workflow artifact is always a zip: unzip it first. The type shown is a guess from the artifact name. A phone cannot do this on its own, so there is no code for a phone.
guide.aab.step1: Turn it into installable APKs with bundletool: bundletool build-apks --connected-device --bundle=app.aab --output=app.apks
guide.aab.step3: Or put the bundle on a Play internal test track and install from Play.
guide.aab.title: An Android App Bundle cannot be installed directly
guide.apk.caution: A workflow artifact is always a zip: unzip it first. The type shown is a guess from the artifact name. A debug or upload-key build cannot update a copy installed from Play (the signatures differ): remove that copy first.
guide.apk.step1: On the phone: scan the code, or download the zip here and unzip it.
guide.apk.step2: Open the APK and allow "Install unknown apps" for the app you opened it from, once.
guide.apk.step3: Or from a computer: adb install app.apk (USB debugging on).
guide.apk.title: Install an Android APK
guide.eas.failedStep: Open the build on Expo to read its log and the reason it failed, fix the cause and build again.
guide.eas.internalCaution: Kiln does not download EAS builds and holds no install link of its own; Expo does.
guide.eas.internalStep1: Open the build on Expo: for a build with internal distribution it has the install link for the device.
guide.eas.internalStepAndroid: On Android the link installs the build (the phone asks to allow installing from this source, once).
guide.eas.internalStepIos: On iOS an internal build only runs on devices that are in its provisioning profile (registered by UDID, or an enterprise profile).
guide.eas.runningStep: Open the build on Expo to follow its progress. This page reads it again every few minutes while it runs.
guide.eas.runningTitle: This EAS build has not finished
guide.eas.simulatorCaution: Kiln does not download EAS builds; Expo does.
guide.eas.simulatorStep1: A simulator build runs in the iOS Simulator on a Mac, not on a phone.
guide.eas.simulatorStep2: Open the build on Expo to download it, then drag it onto a running simulator.
guide.eas.storeStep1: A store distribution build is meant to be sent to the store, not installed from a link.
guide.eas.storeStep2: Submit it with EAS Submit (the submissions below show how that went), or upload it to the store yourself, then test it from TestFlight or Google Play.
guide.ipa.caution: A workflow artifact is always a zip: unzip it first. The type shown is a guess from the artifact name. Installing over the air from a link is not offered: Apple needs a trusted public HTTPS address and a manifest for it.
guide.ipa.step1: An ad hoc or development IPA only runs on devices that are in its provisioning profile (by UDID). Any other device refuses it.
guide.ipa.step2: On a Mac: unzip, connect the device, and drag the IPA onto it in Finder, or use Apple Configurator or Xcode (Window, Devices and Simulators).
guide.ipa.step3: An IPA built for the App Store cannot be installed this way: upload it to TestFlight instead.
guide.ipa.title: Install an iOS IPA
guide.mac.stepApp: Unzip it and move the app to Applications.
guide.mac.stepDmg: Open the DMG and drag the app to Applications.
guide.mac.stepGatekeeper: A downloaded app is checked by Gatekeeper. A notarized build opens normally; one that is not asks you to allow it in System Settings, Privacy and Security, "Open Anyway".
guide.mac.stepPkg: Open the PKG and follow the installer.
guide.mac.title: Install a Mac build
guide.other.step1: This artifact does not look like an app build (a test report, logs or symbols, for example).
guide.other.step2: You can still download it as a zip.
guide.other.title: Not recognised as a build
guide.play.noTrack: No track holds this version code at the moment.
guide.play.step1: Play builds cannot be downloaded as a file here. Testers install from the Play Store.
guide.play.stepInternal: For the internal track, the tester joins with the opt-in link from Play Console (Testing, Internal testing, Testers), then installs from Play.
guide.play.stepOptIn: A tester who was invited to the track opens the opt-in link below on the phone, joins, and installs from Play.
guide.play.title: Install from Google Play
guide.testflight.estimate: A TestFlight build lasts 90 days from its upload; the date shown is that estimate.
guide.testflight.expired: This build has expired and cannot be installed any more.
guide.testflight.processing: Apple is still processing this build; it cannot be installed yet.
guide.testflight.step1: Store builds cannot be downloaded as a file. Open the TestFlight app on the device.
guide.testflight.step2: Internal testers (people in App Store Connect) see a processed build there automatically.
guide.testflight.step3: External testers need an invitation or the public link of a beta group, made in App Store Connect.
guide.testflight.title: Install from TestFlight
guide.zip.step1: Download it and unzip it to see what the workflow uploaded (an IPA, an APK, an AAB or a Mac app).
guide.zip.step2: Then install it as described for that type.
guide.zip.title: A build in a zip
guide.zipNote: A workflow artifact is always a zip: unzip it first. The type shown is a guess from the artifact name.
